title: Introducing Infracost Agents: Find Cloud Waste, Fix It in Code
summary: Infracost Agents scans your cloud estate, investigates waste, and drives fixes through PRs, tickets, and AI coding assistants. Now in private beta.
body_text: One of our design partners was walking through findings surfaced by the new Infracost Idle & Unused Resources agent when she spotted something unexpected: two orphaned load balancers in an account that had just been cleaned up. She clicked the link in the finding, confirmed the resources were still running in AWS and wasting money every day. The agent went beyond just flagging the resources as idle. In it's investigation it identified that the Terraform modules managing these resources had been removed from the codebase, but the live infrastructure was never actually destroyed. "I actually thought everything was removed," she said. "The team must have missed some cleanups." Simple human errors compound — quietly, on your bill, every month. This is the gap that Infracost Agents is built to close. Find issues across your entire cloud estate. Map them to code. Investigate them. Fix them. Reports aren't remediation Cloud cost tools are good at finding problems. They surface dashboards, flag anomalies, and generate reports that tell you exactly where money is being wasted. What they don't do is investigate or fix anything. The finding sits in a list. Someone has to investigate it, trace it back to the right codebase, figure out who owns it, open a PR, get it reviewed, and get it merged. For a FinOps team managing thousands of resources across dozens of accounts, that is not a workflow — it is a backlog that grows faster than anyone can drain it. Infracost Agents is different. It doesn't just find issues in your cloud environment — it traces them back to infrastructure code, investigates them, and drives remediation through the workflows your engineering team already uses: pull requests, tickets, and AI coding assistants. The fix happens where it belongs, in code, so your IaC stays the source of truth and drift doesn't compound. That includes resources that were never in IaC to begin with. ClickOps resources — provisioned directly in the console, outside your Terraform or AWS CDK — have historically been invisible to Infracost. Agents surfaces them too. When it can't trace a resource back to code, it still raises the finding so you can decide how to handle remediation. How it works Agents run scheduled checks against your cloud environment and billing data. When a check detects something wrong — an idle resource, a tagging violation, an anomalous cost spike — it triggers an investigation. The investigation is where the work happens: the agent traces the resource to its IaC, infers ownership, enriches the signal with usage and billing context, and produces a finding with the tasks needed to resolve it. From there, you choose how to act. Have the agent open a PR to fix the issue directly in code — no manual changes, no drift. Route it to your engineering backlog as a Jira or Linear ticket, pre-populated with the agent's investigation. Or hand off its findings to your AI coding assistant so you or a developer on your team can collaborate on a fix. Every decision you make teaches the agent. Dismiss a finding because that idle load balancer is tied to a roadmap project that isn't live yet? The agent records that context and won't surface it again until something changes. Over time, the agents get smarter about your environment, your policies, and your team's intent. The first three agents Infracost Agents launches in private beta with three agents: Idle and Unused Resources monitors your cloud estate for resources consuming spend without delivering value — idle EC2 instances, unattached volumes, load balancers with no traffic, clusters with no workloads. It also surfaces orphaned resources that have been removed from code but never destroyed in the cloud. For each finding, it traces the resource to its IaC and opens a removal PR when you're ready. Tagging enforces your tag policies at scale. It scans both IaC-managed and manually created resources, identifies violations, and opens PRs to fix them in code. For resources outside IaC, it flags them explicitly so you know what's drifted from policy. Cost Anomaly Detection ingests anomalies from AWS and thoroughly investigates them — correlating spikes to application and infrastructure changes, identifying the likely root cause, and surfacing the context your team needs to act before the cost compounds. These are the first three. More agents are in development, covering areas like Kubernetes rightsizing, AI cost optimization, and compute right-sizing. Private beta gives you a seat at the table as we build them. What private beta means Infracost Agents is in active development. Private beta customers get hands-on access to the product, direct input into roadmap priorities, and a dedicated channel with the Infracost team. We're looking for engineering and FinOps teams who are serious about reducing cloud waste and willing to help shape what this becomes. If that's you, join the waitlist. We'll reach out when Infracost Agents is ready for your environment. Join the waitlist → Already an Infracost customer? Contact your account team to discuss private beta eligibility.

title: Your Face Closes the Deal Before You Say Anything
summary: What a professional headshot photographer actually delivers, what a good headshot costs you to skip, and how to book quality headshots at scale.
body_text: The Tenth of a Second That Follows You Everywhere Someone lands on your LinkedIn profile, your team page, or your speaker bio. Their brain has already decided whether you look competent and trustworthy, and it happened faster than they can consciously register. Princeton psychologists Janine Willis and Alexander Todorov found that people form those judgments after just a tenth of a second of looking at a face , and that more time to study the face only made them more confident, not more accurate. Trust was among the judgments viewers formed fastest. In other words, the photo is doing the talking, and it never stops. That is the case for hiring a professional headshot photographer rather than cropping yourself out of a wedding photo. Here is what a good one delivers, what it is worth, and how to do it at scale. What you are actually paying for A genuine smile was the biggest single lift to how likable you read. A phone can capture a face. What it cannot do is control the variables that move perception, and those variables are measurable. Photo-rating platform PhotoFeeler ran the numbers on this. In a study built on more than 60,000 ratings of 800 business profile photos , the strongest factor for likability was a genuine smile with teeth visible, worth an average lift of 1.35 points on their scale. Formal dress drove the largest gains in perceived competence and influence, while sunglasses and shadowed eyes dragged scores down. A skilled photographer directs all of this live: the squint that reads as confidence instead of fear, the jawline, the lighting that keeps your eyes clear. That is the difference between a photographer who knows why a shot works and a friend hoping one of forty frames lands. Curious how your current photo reads on those same traits? Snappr's free Photo Analyzer scores it in seconds. As we covered in why your headshot is a key component of personal branding , the image is a deliberate business asset, not a formality. The cost of a bad one Skipping the professional route carries a price you pay later. Recruiters move fast. An eye-tracking study conducted by TheLadders found that recruiters spend roughly six seconds scanning a resume before deciding whether to keep reading, and online that snap judgment includes your photo. Employers are looking, too: a CareerBuilder survey found 70% of employers research candidates on social media, and 57% of them rejected someone based on what they found , with inappropriate photos the most common trigger. The photo is not decoration. It is evidence. Even the C-suite is not exempt. Snappr's look at the Fortune 500 CEOs with the best and worst headshots shows how many leaders still get the basics wrong. The upside runs the other way too. Snappr's own analysis found that professional headshots increase perceived trust and credibility by 78% . For a salesperson, a founder raising a round, or a consultant sending a proposal, that lift compounds across every first impression. When one headshot becomes fifty For an individual, booking a professional headshot photographer is a solved problem: find someone local, sit for an hour, get your files. The real challenge shows up at scale. A company that wants consistent headshots across a sales team, a leadership page, or a distributed workforce hits a different beast: sourcing photographers in every city, briefing each one so lighting and background match, chasing files, and re-shooting the person who joined last month. Do it ad hoc and your team page looks like a ransom note of mismatched styles. As we noted in why your startup's team photos can make or break your image , inconsistency reads as amateur even when each individual photo is fine. This is what Snappr was built to solve. You set your shoot guidelines once, and Snappr applies them to every session across a network covering 95% of the United States. You can book a vetted professional headshot photographer in about two minutes, on 24 hours' notice, and photos come back professionally edited within a day or two. One brief, one consistent look, whether it is one new hire or two hundred people across four offices. Snappr's business portraits service runs the coordination so your team does not have to. The takeaway A professional headshot photographer is not buying a nicer picture. It is buying control over a judgment that happens in a tenth of a second and repeats every time someone finds you online. For one person, that is worth an hour. For a team, it is worth a system. If you are standardizing headshots across a company, talk to Snappr's enterprise team about running your team's photography as one managed program. Frequently Asked Questions What does a professional headshot photographer do that I can't do myself? A professional headshot photographer controls lighting, angle, expression, and framing to shape how competent and trustworthy you appear. Research shows specific, controllable factors like a genuine smile and clear eyes measurably change how viewers rate a photo, and directing those in the moment is the skill you are paying for. How quickly do people judge a headshot? Almost instantly. Princeton research found that people form impressions of trustworthiness and competence from a face in about a tenth of a second, and extra viewing time only increases their confidence in that first read rather than changing it. Do professional headshots actually affect hiring and business outcomes? Yes. Recruiters scan a resume in roughly six seconds, and surveys show most employers research candidates online and reject some based on what they find, with inappropriate photos a leading cause. On the positive side, Snappr's analysis found professional headshots raise perceived trust and credibility by 78%. How do companies book a professional headshot photographer for a whole team? The reliable approach is to set shoot guidelines once and apply them to every session, rather than briefing a new photographer each time. Snappr does this across its network covering 95% of the US, so a distributed team gets one consistent look on one timeline instead of a patchwork of styles. Sources 1. title: Five Metrics to Check Before Buying a Dividend Stock
summary: Five metrics to check before buying a dividend stock offer investors seeking reliable passive income a screening process.
body_text: Five Metrics to Check Before Buying a Dividend Stock By: Jonathan Wolfgram , July 9, 2026 Link copied! Five metrics to check before buying a dividend stock offer investors seeking reliable passive income a screening process. The five metrics to check before buying a dividend stock, especially any high dividend stocks with a consistent payout, will help empower investors to make wise, profitable decisions. Virtually every week, DividendInvestor.com provides new recommendations for the best dividend stocks to add to your portfolio, but it helps to use online tools to invest wisely. The first half of that equation comes in screening for dividend stocks — both the Dividend Screener on DividendInvestor.com and the platform designed by our partners at Stock Rover are excellent tools for investors to gather the data they need. Interpreting that data, however, is a challenge in itself. That’s why, starting with the basics, we compiled a list of the five metrics to check before buying a dividend stock. This article will tell you what these metrics are, where they come from and what they mean for practical, profitable investing. 5 Metrics to Check Before Buying A Dividend Stock: Dividends Per Share Dividends per share is the first and most fundamental of the dividend metrics. When a company decides to reward its shareholders by distributing a dividend, it sets aside a specific amount of a company’s money for every outstanding share, or dividends per share . For every share of the company you own, you’ll receive a payout equal to the dividends per share multiplied by however many shares are in your portfolio. Take the dividends per share of 3M ( NYSE:MMM ) as an example: Data provided by Stock Rover , learn more about the online tool here . While there are dividends that payout annually or monthly, the vast majority of dividend payers distribute on a quarterly basis. In 2021, 3M paid a dividend per share of $1.48 every quarter, meaning for every share of MMM you owned, you would have received $5.92 by year’s end. For example, let’s say you owned 100 shares of MMM. In 2021 alone, the company would have paid you $592.00 in dividend distributions. Advertisement. 5 Metrics to Check Before Buying A Dividend Stock: Dividend Yield A $592.00 check just for owning some stock sounds nice until you realize that 100 shares of 3M, at their current price, cost $14,175.00. That’s where dividend yield comes in, which effectively measures the efficiency of your investment — dividend yield tells you how much you can expect to be paid relative to the amount of money you invest. To find the dividend yield, we use the following formula: Let’s use 3M as an example again. Looking back to the data table above, we see that 3M pays a dividend of $1.49 per share per quarter, equivalent to an annual dividend of $5.96 per share. We divide that number by the share price as of as of August 3, 2022, $141.75, and get:: So 3M has a forward dividend yield of 4.2%, meaning for every $100 you invest in the company, you’ll receive a dividend distribution of $4.20. However, many investors stop there, thinking that in order to make the best investments, they need only find the stocks with the highest dividend yields! Not so fast. A closer look at the formula shows us that two things will make the dividend yield larger: high dividend distributions — which are good — but also falling share prices . Many high-yielding companies are those that may have paid a fair dividend in the last year but since then have seen their stock price plummet. If a share price changes suddenly, it may take several months for the financial defeat to be reflected in historical dividends. A company may have paid a nice dividend three months ago, but if it went belly-up since then, the dividend yield will appear unnaturally high. Dividend yield is an important metric, but it’s for this reason that it cannot stand alone. To evaluate the actual performance of a company as a dividend payer, we need to look past high yields and evaluate a company’s fundamentals. 5 Metrics to Check Before Buying A Dividend Stock: Dividend Growth Rate For long-term investors, a stock’s dividend growth rate is arguably more important than its yield. A high yield will reward investors in the short-term, but if it drops gradually over time, investors may be sorely disappointed in their waning returns. Even if the dividend distribution stays constant, inflation will gradually eat away at investors’ profits as the equity becomes less viable over time. That’s why it’s important for dividend-paying companies to be growing their dividend distributions, both to keep ahead of inflation and to reward their long-term investors. Dividend increases may be seen every period or perhaps just on an annual basis, but we track the average growth rate over a multi-year period. Data provided by StockRover , start your free trial here . Advertisement. In the case of 3M, we see that the company has not consistently increased its dividend. 5 Metrics to Check Before Buying A Dividend Stock: Consecutive Dividend Increases Investors with a strong focus on long-term reliability of income may look to consecutive dividend increases to evaluate their stock picks. Consecutive dividend increases as a metric is exactly that — how many years in a row the company has increased its dividend distribution. Dropping a dividend or even keeping it level for a year resets a company’s streak to zero. Our example stock, MMM, has increased its dividend distribution 64 years in a row. This makes it a member of the Dividend Aristocrats — an elite group of S&P 500 companies that have increased their dividend payouts 25 or more years in a row. 3M is also a member of an even more exclusive group of companies called the Dividend Kings , a title reserved for companies with consecutive dividend increases of 50 or more. Dividend Aristocrats and Kings, as well as other equities with uber-high consecutive dividend increases, are stable investments. A long streak of increasing dividend distributions not only shows a company’s ability to weather financial challenges and the ups and downs of the market but demonstrates a continued optimism for the future of the company. That said, there are plenty of strong dividend investments without long consecutive dividend increase streaks, but the Dividend Aristocrats and Dividend Kings serve as excellent starting points for investors hoping to stabilize their portfolios. 5 Metrics to Check Before Buying A Dividend Stock: Dividend Payout Ratio Dividend growth and consecutive dividend increases offer historical data points for analysts and investors to estimate the likelihood of a company cutting its dividend, but the dividend payout ratio serves a similar purpose on a more current basis. The dividend payout ratio informs investors how much of a company’s profits are distributed as dividends, or rather, how what percentage of overall profit is being given back to shareholders. It is calculated using the following formula: Lower dividend payout ratios are considered safer since the company will be able to continue its dividend payments should it be met with financial difficulties. Additionally, it often means the company is reinvesting a substantial share of its profits back into its own growth. This does, however, mean less money in the shareholders’ pockets. A payout ratio between 35 and 55% is generally considered good — enough that shareholders are making a meaningful profit, but not so much that the company may become unable to pay its dividend in the near future. Payout ratios much higher may indicate that a company may be headed towards a dividend cut to bring its distributions back into a sustainable range. Advertisement. An exception to this rule is real estate investment trusts (REIT). For information on how to evaluate a REIT’s payout ratio, read our article on the topic here . 3M has a dividend payout ratio of 63%, meaning for every dollar the company makes, $0.63 of it is being distributed back to shareholders. This is only slightly above what is considered the sustainable range, but since the company also maintains high dividend growth and a long streak of consecutive dividend increases, we can assume the dividend is safe despite this. title: Greg Smith Shares Real-World Lessons on the SunCast Podcast
summary: Greg Smith, Tigo's Global Director of Learning, joined Nico Johnson on the SunCast Podcast for a candid conversation from NABCEP 2026 about the mistakes that cause the most common solar service issues and how they can be prevented long before an installer arrives on the roof.
body_text: Greg Smith , Tigo's Global Director of Learning, joined Nico Johnson on the SunCast Podcast for a candid conversation from NABCEP 2026 about the mistakes that cause the most common solar service issues and how they can be prevented long before an installer arrives on the roof. ‍ Better System Design Starts Before Installation One of Greg's biggest takeaways is that many of the industry's most expensive problems originate during system design - not during installation. Thoughtful equipment selection, proper system planning, and attention to installation details help prevent callbacks and ensure systems perform as expected over their lifetime. ‍ "A lot of this boils down to what I've coined over the years: RTFM - Read the Fun Manual. We analyzed our service calls, and about 30% of them come down to people simply not reading the documentation." - Greg Smith ‍ Set the Right Homeowner Expectations Greg also emphasizes the importance of educating homeowners before installation begins. From understanding battery backup capabilities to discussing critical load panels and backup duration, setting realistic expectations leads to better customer experiences and fewer surprises during grid outages. ‍ Communication Is Key to Long-Term Reliability As solar systems become more connected, Greg explains that communication issues have become one of the industry's most common service calls. Proper component placement, careful commissioning, and following installation best practices can significantly improve long-term system reliability while reducing unnecessary truck rolls. ‍ ‍ Whether you're designing systems, installing equipment, or helping homeowners understand their investment, Greg's conversation offers valuable insights into building solar systems that perform reliably for years to come. ‍ Watch the full episode of the SunCast Podcast to hear Greg's practical lessons from nearly two decades in the solar industry.

summary: Dime Commercial Bancshares, Inc. Reports 17% Year-Over-Year Increase in EPS...
body_text: Net Interest Margin Expansion Drives Record Quarterly Revenue of $126 million; Strong Year-Over-Year Core Deposit and Business Loan Growth Announces Plans to Resume Share Buybacks HAUPPAUGE, N.Y., July 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Dime Commercial Bancshares, Inc. (NYSE: DCOM) (the “Company” or “Dime”), the parent company of Dime Commercial Bank (the “Bank”), today reported net income available to common stockholders of $33.0 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, or $0.75 per diluted common share, compared to net income available to common stockholders of $32.8 million, or $0.75 per diluted common share, for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 and net income available to common stockholders of $27.9 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2025, or $0.64 per diluted common share. Adjusted net income available to common stockholders (non-GAAP) was $34.7 million and adjusted diluted EPS (non-GAAP) was $0.79 per share for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared to $0.74 per share for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 and $0.64 for the quarter ended June 30, 2025 (see "Non-GAAP Reconciliation" tables at the end of this news release). Stuart H. Lubow, President and Chief Executive Officer (“CEO”) of the Company, stated, “Dime continues to execute on our growth plan and delivered record quarterly revenue. Second quarter results were marked by strong growth in business loans as our commercial banking teams are converting their robust pipelines. Recognizing the progress we have made in creating a high-quality balance sheet, Kroll Bond Rating Agency recently issued a “Positive” ratings outlook for Dime. Finally, and in recognition of our evolution into a commercial and private banking powerhouse, we recently completed our re-brand to “Dime Commercial Bank”.” Capital Return : Mr. Lubow, stated, “In light of our strong capital position, lower CRE concentration levels, stress testing results, and improving profitability, we are pleased to announce that we expect to begin repurchasing our shares in the third quarter.” Highlights for the Second Quarter of 2026 included: Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.79 per share for the second quarter of 2026, compared to $0.64 per share for the second quarter of 2025; Total deposits increased $937.0 million on a year-over-year basis; Core deposits (excluding brokered and time deposits) increased $948.3 million on a year-over-year basis; Average non-interest-bearing deposits to average total deposits for the second quarter increased to 31.0%; Business loans grew $280.8 million on a linked quarter basis and $743.0 million on a year-over-year basis; The net interest margin increased to 3.28% for the second quarter of 2026 compared to 3.21% for the prior quarter; The efficiency ratio decreased to 51.2% for the second quarter of 2026 compared to 55.0% for second quarter of 2025; The adjusted efficiency ratio decreased to 49.9% for the second quarter of 2026 compared to 54.7% for the second quarter of 2025; The Company’s Tier 1 Common Equity Ratio increased to 11.99% at the end of the second quarter; The Company’s Consolidated CRE Concentration ratio was proactively managed lower to 352%; and Non-performing assets declined by 28% on a linked quarter basis and represented 0.46% of Total Assets. Management’s Discussion of Quarterly Operating Results Net Interest Income Net interest income for the second quarter of 2026 was $115.2 million compared to $112.3 million for the first quarter of 2026 and $98.1 million for the second quarter of 2025. The Net Interest Margin for the second quarter of 2026 was 3.28% compared to 3.21% for the first quarter of 2026 and 2.98% for the second quarter of 2025. Mr. Lubow commented, “We continue to have a significant loan repricing opportunity that we anticipate will continue through 2027. Additionally, growth in core deposits and business loans will benefit us over time as we continue to grow our customer base. Our substantial liquidity position, which includes $1.9 billion of cash, provides us with the flexibility to take advantage of lending opportunities as they arise. Dime’s asset liability management profile, which is underpinned by our cash position and a growing floating rate loan portfolio, positions us well for a variety of interest rate scenarios.” Loan Portfolio The ending weighted average rate (“WAR”) on the total loan portfolio was 5.36% at June 30, 2026, an 8-basis point increase compared to the ending WAR of 5.28% on the total loan portfolio at March 31, 2026. Excluding the fair value change in equity securities and loans held for sale, and loss (gain) on sale of securities, loans and other assets, non-interest income was $13.2 million during the second quarter of 2026, $11.7 million during the first quarter of 2026 and $11.4 million during the second quarter of 2025. Non-Interest Expense Total non-interest expense was $64.7 million during the second quarter of 2026, $62.8 million during the first quarter of 2026, and $60.3 million during the second quarter of 2025. Excluding the impact of the net loss (gain) on extinguishment of debt, amortization of other intangible assets and severance expense, adjusted non-interest expense was $64.1 million during the second quarter of 2026, $63.4 million during the first quarter of 2026, and $59.9 million during the second quarter of 2025 (see “Non-GAAP Reconciliation” tables at the end of this news release). The ratio of non-interest expense to average assets was 1.74% during the second quarter of 2026, compared to 1.68% during the linked quarter and 1.72% during the second quarter of 2025. Excluding the impact of the net loss (gain) on extinguishment of debt, amortization of other intangible assets and severance expense, the ratio of adjusted non-interest expense to average assets was 1.72% during the second quarter of 2026, 1.69% during the first quarter of 2026, and 1.71% during the second quarter of 2025 (see “Non-GAAP Reconciliation” tables at the end of this news release). The efficiency ratio was 51.2% during the second quarter of 2026, compared to 50.8% during the linked quarter and 55.0% during the second quarter of 2025. Excluding the impact of loss (gain) on sale of securities, loans and other assets, fair value change in equity securities and loans held for sale, severance expense, net loss (gain) on extinguishment of debt, and amortization of other intangible assets, the adjusted efficiency ratio was 49.9% during the second quarter of 2026, compared to 51.2% during the linked quarter and 54.7% during the second quarter of 2025 (see “Non-GAAP Reconciliation” tables at the end of this news release). Mr. Lubow commented, “Our organic growth strategy is paying dividends as evidenced by a decline in the core efficiency ratio to below 50% for the second quarter. Growth in revenues is anticipated to continue to drive the efficiency ratio lower in the years ahead.” Income Tax Expense Income tax expense was $13.1 million during the second quarter of 2026, $13.9 million during the first quarter of 2026, and $10.5 million during the second quarter of 2025. The effective tax rate for the second quarter of 2026 was 27.3%, compared to 28.7% for the first quarter of 2026 and 26.1% for the second quarter of 2025. Credit Quality Non-performing assets were $69.0 million at June 30, 2026, compared to $95.6 million at March 31, 2026 and $53.2 million at June 30, 2025. A credit loss provision of $13.9 million was recorded during the second quarter of 2026, compared to $12.3 million during the first quarter of 2026, and $9.2 million during the second quarter of 2025. Capital Management Stockholders’ equity increased $23.5 million to $1.52 billion at June 30, 2026, compared to $1.50 billion at March 31, 2026. The Company’s and the Bank’s regulatory capital ratios continued to be in excess of all applicable regulatory requirements as of June 30, 2026. All risk-based regulatory capital ratios increased during the second quarter of 2026. Dividends per common share were $0.25 during the second quarter of 2026 and the first quarter of 2026, respectively. Book value per common share was $31.79 at June 30, 2026 compared to $31.33 at March 31, 2026. Tangible common book value per share (which represents common equity less goodwill and other intangible assets, divided by the number of shares outstanding) was $28.21 at June 30, 2026 compared to $27.73 at March 31, 2026 (see “Non-GAAP Reconciliation” tables at the end of this news release). title: UK Leads Europe Ransomware Attacks: Cyble Q1 2026 Report
summary: Cyble report reveals UK as Europe’s top ransomware target in Q1 2026, with five groups driving 60% of attacks and manufacturing sectors most affected.
body_text: UK tops Europe's ransomware target list as five groups take 60% of attacks, new Cyble report finds Manufacturing and construction overtake financial services; British aerospace firm and European Space Agency among Q1 victims LONDON— April 22, 2026 — The United Kingdom was the most-attacked country in Europe for ransomware in the first quarter of 2026, according to the Europe Threat Landscape Report: Q1 2026 published today by Cyble. Across the region, Cyble Research and Intelligence Labs (CRIL) recorded 462 major cyber incidents between January and March, including 404 ransomware attacks, 51 data breaches, and seven listings for the sale of compromised network access. The report’s central finding is the degree to which both the ransomware market and the underground market for initial access have consolidated. Five ransomware groups — Qilin, The Gentlemen, Akira, NightSpire, and LockBit — were collectively responsible for approximately 60% of the 404 ransomware attacks observed across Europe in the quarter. Qilin alone claimed 87 attacks, more than one in five of the total. On the dark web , two brokers — known as tamnaamm and algoyim — accounted for 71% of all observed sales of compromised access into European organisations. For the past four years CISOs have been told that ransomware is an ecosystem of thousands of actors and that defence is a game of chance,” said Kaustubh Medhe, CTO & VP – Research and Threat Intelligence of Cyble . “This quarter’s data shows the opposite. Five groups and two access brokers are driving the majority of the activity hitting Europe. That gives security leaders something they haven’t had: a short, named list of adversaries to prioritise detection engineering, threat hunts, and board-level briefings against.” The report also documents a pronounced shift in sector targeting. Manufacturing and construction were the two most-attacked sectors, displacing financial services. Cyble attributes this to a deliberate adversary calculation: manufacturers and construction firms carry narrow operational tolerance for downtime, which shortens the time between intrusion and ransom payment. “Threat groups have worked out where the pressure point is,” added Kaustubh. “A factory that loses three days of production faces contract penalties, supply-chain breakage, and in some cases existential loss. Banks have mature incident response, cyber insurance, and regulators watching. Adversaries are price-discriminating on willingness to pay, and the data shows it is working.” Key findings from the report 462 cyber incidents observed across Europe in Q1 2026, including 404 ransomware attacks , 51 data breaches and leaks , and seven initial-access sales . Qilin was the most active ransomware group, responsible for 87 incidents (over 21% of all ransomware activity) , followed by The Gentlemen (58) , Akira (42) , NightSpire (27) , and LockBit (26) . Manufacturing and construction were the most-targeted sectors, overtaking financial services. The United Kingdom was the most-attacked country for ransomware in the quarter, followed by Germany, Italy, and France, separated by single-digit margins. A UK aeronautical fabrication firm was breached by Interlock Group on 6 January, with aerospace drawings and employee contract data claimed as exfiltrated. The European Space Agency was compromised on 8 January by a threat actor operating as “888”, with the group targeting collaborative engineering servers used by the scientific community. A database containing the personal records of 5,851,232 French diploma holders was advertised for sale on a cybercrime forum. A critical zero-day in Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile (CVE-2026-1340, CVSS 9.8) was weaponised shortly after disclosure; CRIL attributes exploitation activity to nation-state actors including Sandworm / APT28 . Separate critical flaws in Dell RecoverPoint (CVE-2026-22769, CVSS 10.0) and Cisco Secure Firewall Management Centre (CVE-2026-20131) were also observed in active exploitation. Pro-Russian hacktivist collectives , most notably NoName057(16), have extended their activity from DDoS campaigns into claimed administrative access to Industrial Control Systems, including water treatment and supply, heating plants, and a mini-hydroelectric facility. UK government and airport websites were among the targets of the DDoS campaigns. Sustained nation-state espionage continued, with the Salt Typhoon campaign targeting telecommunications providers globally. What this means for UK and European CISOs Cyble’s guidance to security leaders reading the report is to treat Q1 2026 as an opportunity to narrow the defensive aperture. A short adversary list allows organisations to align detection coverage, tabletop exercises, and insurer conversations against a specific set of groups rather than a diffuse threat surface. Manufacturers and construction firms — together with their downstream supply chains — should assume they are above-baseline targets, and should accelerate OT/IT segmentation reviews, back-up restoration testing, and patch programmes for edge infrastructure. Organisations running Ivanti EPMM, Dell RecoverPoint, or Cisco Secure Firewall Management Centre should treat this quarter’s CVEs as priority-one remediation. The report arrives ahead of the UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill and against the backdrop of NIS2 enforcement across the EU, both of which place sharper obligations on operators of essential services — precisely the sectors most heavily targeted in the quarter. About the report Europe Threat Landscape: Q1 2026 is a 31-page analysis covering ransomware, data breaches, initial access sales, vulnerability intelligence, and hacktivism. It is available for free, without registration, here . About Cyble Cyble is an AI-native cybersecurity company providing unified risk intelligence and decision support to enterprises worldwide. Powered by BlazeAI , Cyble’s platform integrates data, advanced reasoning, and automation to enable organisations to respond faster and more confidently. Recognised as a top-rated solution on Gartner Peer Insights, Cyble is praised for its actionable insights and robust platform capabilities. For more information, visit www.cyble.com . title: Collection Letter Templates & Strategies to Get Paid Faster
summary: Explore collection letter templates, learn what to include, and build a strategy to recover overdue invoices and prevent late payments.
body_text: Collection Letter Templates & Strategies to Get Paid Faster AR collections Payment reminders Alexandre Antoine Jul 10, 2026 Summary What is a Collection Letter? How to Create a Collection Strategy What to include in a Collection Letter? Collection Letter Templates How to Prevent Late Payments Early On? FAQs Collection letters are one of the most effective ways to recover overdue invoices when payment reminders and phone calls go unanswered. They provide a structured and professional way to follow up on late payments, increase urgency, and protect customer relationships while ensuring you get paid. Whether you're creating your first collection process or refining an existing one, having the right approach and templates in place can make a significant difference in how quickly you collect payments. Keep reading to explore: What is a Collection Letter? How to Create a Collection Strategy What to Include in a Collection Letter? Collection Letter Templates How to Prevent Late Payments Early On? Want to prevent late payments from reaching the stage of collection letters? Click the banner below to connect with our cash collection experts and build a personalized strategy for your business. What is a Collection Letter? A collection letter is a formal written notice sent to a customer or client who has an overdue or outstanding invoice . Its purpose is to remind the debtor of the due payment, establish a sense of urgency, and provide a clear request for the balance to be settled. Unlike the initial friendly reminders, collection notices or letters typically signal a more serious stage in the accounts receivable process , especially when prior email reminders or phone calls have gone unanswered. Collection letters often escalate in tone over time, from polite initial requests to firmer demands as the delinquency period increases. They may also outline potential consequences of non-payment, such as late fees, service disruptions, or legal action. Businesses typically send these letters after exhausting softer communication approaches, but before taking formal legal action. A well-structured collection letter should include details such as the amount due, invoice number, payment terms, deadline for payment, and instructions on how to resolve the matter. It is always advised to send polite collection emails before moving towards collection letters. Click on the banner below to download our free collection email templates How to Create a Collection Strategy A successful cash collection strategy is about balancing assertiveness with maintaining positive customer relationships. Emilie Hart and the team at WorkMotion epitomise this approach. Emilie, who leads the Finance Operations Team, notes: “Our main goal is to create a positive customer experience when it comes to collections by ensuring we’re sending and triggering reminders when it matters most”. By tailoring the payment experience to individual customers, using segmentation and contextual knowledge from past interactions, Upflow ensures businesses like WorkMotion are able to engage the right person at the right time and place, specifically within the finance pillar of the customer journey. It’s an approach we call Financial Relationship Management . But what are the common steps in a cash collection strategy? It generally begins with a friendly reminder a few days before the due date, followed by another on the due date. Once the invoice has passed its due date, the first set of email reminders should be polite and gentle, assuming the delay might be unintentional. The goal is to prompt payment without damaging rapport. If the first reminder after the due date fails to generate a response, the second and third communications should gradually become more assertive. By the third outreach, it may be time to escalate the situation by introducing phone calls, which allow for more direct interaction and quicker resolution. Phone calls also create a more personal connection, showing that you’re serious about receiving payment but still value the relationship. If emails and phone calls do not yield results, the next step is to send collection letters . These formal collection notices indicate urgency, making it clear that further delays may result in more serious actions. The final escalation is often a legal notice , indicating that the debt will be pursued through legal channels if it remains unpaid. This step should only be taken as a last resort, after all reasonable attempts to collect the debt have been exhausted. What to include in a Collection Letter? A well-crafted collection letter helps ensure clarity and urgency while maintaining professionalism. Here’s what you should include: Personal Information : Address the letter directly to the recipient, including their full name, company name, and any details about the services or products you’ve provided. This personal touch not only ensures that the letter reaches the right person but also reminds them of your relationship and the value your business has delivered. Your Contact Information : Provide multiple ways for the recipient to contact you. Include your business address, email, and phone number, making it easy for them to resolve the payment issue or get in touch with any questions. Attach All Overdue Invoices : Always include copies of all overdue invoices . This ensures the client has a clear view of each outstanding balance, including invoice numbers, amounts due, and due dates. If there are multiple invoices, create a concise list in the body of the letter to ensure transparency and avoid confusion. Invoice Details and Due Date : Reference the original invoice numbers, the amount owed, and the number of days past due. Emphasize this information to highlight the urgency of the situation and remind them of the missed deadlines. Updated Invoice with Late Fees (If Applicable) : If your business charges late fees , include an updated invoice reflecting the additional charges. Make sure to clarify that the late fee will continue to accumulate if the payment is further delayed, depending on your terms and conditions. Payment Methods : Provide clear and convenient payment options. List all acceptable payment methods such as credit card, bank transfer, or online payment links. The easier it is for the client to pay, the quicker you’ll receive payment. Providing a direct payment link can significantly speed up the process. Offer a Payment Plan (Optional) : If applicable, offer the option of a payment plan. This is particularly helpful if the client is struggling financially. Outline potential terms for weekly or monthly payments, making it easier for them to manage the overdue balance. Consequences of Non-Payment : Detail the next steps if payment isn’t made within a specified time frame. This could include suspending services, transferring the debt to a receivable management services company, or taking legal action. Mention any contractual terms that support these actions, such as late fees or penalties. Be clear but professional when outlining these potential consequences. By including all these elements, your collection letter remains clear, actionable, and professional, maximizing the chances of payment without harming your business relationship. Collection Letter Templates A well-timed series of collection letters can help recover debts without damaging client relationships. Below are four collection letter template samples that escalate from a polite reminder to a formal legal notice, helping guide the communication process and ensure timely payment. Formal Reminder of Due Payment: Collection Letter Template 1 This first letter is a polite reminder following previous communication (emails, phone calls or even SMS ) about overdue payments. It provides a clear summary of the outstanding invoices, includes payment details, and gently urges the client to take immediate action to avoid further escalation. Warning of Service Restriction: Collection Letter Template 2 This collection notice escalates the situation by warning the client that if payment is not received within a specified timeframe, their access to services or products will be restricted. The tone is more assertive, and it signals the seriousness of the situation, encouraging the client to pay promptly to avoid service disruption. Service Restricted & Legal Warning: Collection Letter Template 3 In this letter, the service has been restricted due to non-payment, and the client is informed of this. The collection notice is more of a warning for a legal notice as it also includes a firm warning about potential legal action if the payment is not made within the given timeframe. The tone remains professional but is more urgent and direct. Legal Notice: Collection Letter Template 4 This final letter is used when legal action has already been initiated due to continued non-payment. It informs the client of the legal steps taken and emphasizes the consequences, urging them to settle the debt to avoid further legal complications or costs. How to Prevent Late Payments Early On? Preventing late payments starts well before invoices are overdue, with a combination of clear communication, strong client relationships, and efficient processes. By taking proactive steps and utilizing automation tools, businesses can minimize the risk of escalating to the point of sending collection letters. Here's how you can prevent late payments: Set Clear Payment Terms: Establishing clear payment terms upfront is key to avoiding late payments. Clearly define due dates, accepted payment methods, and any penalties for delays in the contract. This ensures both parties are on the same page from the beginning. Send Proactive Reminders: Instead of waiting until a payment is overdue, send timely, friendly reminders. Tools like Upflow allow you to automate these reminders, customizing the tone and frequency without needing to write the same email over and over. Upflow even reminds you when it’s time to send a reminder. Offer Flexible Payment Options: The easier it is for clients to pay, the faster they’ll settle their invoices. Offering multiple payment options, such as credit cards, bank transfers, or ACH ensures you’re catering to their preferences and speeding up the process. Automate Payment Processes: Automating your collection and payment reminders with software like Upflow means fewer manual tasks and fewer errors. Upflow integrates seamlessly with your billing, accounting, ERP and CRM systems, ensuring that you always have the latest information at your fingertips without having to manually update spreadsheets or chase after invoices. Segment Your Client Base for Better Focus: While automating reminders helps streamline processes, some clients need personalized attention. Upflow allows you to group clients based on their payment history, making it easier to focus on those who may need a phone call or more personalized outreach, while automating the rest. Incentivize Early Payments: Encourage prompt payments by offering small incentives, such as discounts for early payment . This gives clients extra motivation to pay before the due date, improving your cash flow. Utilize Real-Time Dashboards: Upflow also offers real-time dashboards that give you a clear view of your accounts receivable, enabling you to take swift action when needed. With all your data centralized, you can monitor payment statuses, track overdue accounts, and ensure you’re not caught off-guard by unpaid invoices. Provide a Dedicated Payment Portal: A dedicated payment portal for each customer, like the one offered by Upflow, makes it easy for your clients to settle their accounts, helping you get paid faster without constant back-and-forths. Focus on Strategic Actions: Automating repetitive tasks frees up your team’s time to focus on higher-value activities that can move your business forward. With less time spent chasing payments, your team can dedicate their efforts to nurturing key client relationships and driving growth. By integrating Upflow into your accounts receivable process, you can streamline payment collection, reduce the risk of overdue invoices, and maintain stronger client relationships, all while ensuring that your business runs more efficiently.
